And after another space of time during which Baidu slept,
Gaikhatu again sent the nobles to ask him
if he knew what he had spoken in his drunkenness.
He, however, denied it all the more,
and imagined that he did not even feel whether he had been beaten with stripes.
And he craftily adjured the nobles,
whether they were telling the truth in their account,
or were merely jesting with him.
And when they related before him the whole affair that had taken place between him and Gaikhatu,
he was seized with great astonishment and said:
"Truly there is no equal to Gaikhatu's love for me! Otherwise, how did he not cut me {OCR?} limb from limb in that very hour?"
And when Gaikhatu heard these things,
his mind was very greatly pacified.
And he went to him in person,
and embraced him and kissed him,
and took him and went to the camp,
and brought royal garments and clothed him.
And he showed himself as an offender, an evildoer, and one worthy of death;
and he sighed over the drunkenness, and said weeping:
"I do not know that I have offended;
therefore, if I have offended unknowingly,
and have displeased you unintentionally,
I beg of you,
feed my flesh to your dogs without pity."
Gaikhatu, however, loved him all the more,
and multiplied giving him incomparable gifts.
And in a word,
in these two or three days he bestowed upon Baidu nearly forty myriads,
gold and silver,
and garments woven with gold,
and choice robes,
and belts set with rubies and precious stones,
and riding-beasts, and mules, and horses.
And although Gaikhatu was reproved by all his intimates, who said to him:
"It was not right that the honour of this man should be profaned,
nor that he should be despised to this extent,
and delivered into the hands of base {OCR?} men to drag him by his hair, and scourge him, and wound him.
Now that what has happened has happened,
gifts are of no avail,
nor do flatteries profit.
It is only right to beware of him immediately,
in whatever way it may be."
